Homepage.info: The Red Star Fencing Club was founded to promote and develop fencing in Serbia and quickly became the leading center for this sport. The club has produced many top athletes who have achieved significant results in national and international competitions, fostering team spirit, perseverance, and dedication to fencing.

Weapons.saber_description: The saber is a cutting and thrusting weapon that targets the entire body above the waist, including the head and arms. Saber fencing is the fastest of the three disciplines, characterized by explosive attacks, dynamic footwork, and right-of-way rules that reward aggressive initiative.
Weapons.epee_description: The epee is a thrusting weapon where the entire body is the valid target area. There are no right-of-way rules -- the first fencer to land a touch scores. Epee fencing rewards patience, precise timing, and tactical defensive play.
Weapons.foil_description: The foil is a thrusting weapon that targets the torso (front and back). Foil fencing uses right-of-way rules, requiring fencers to establish priority through their attack before scoring. It emphasizes technique, blade work, and strategic exchanges.
Weapons.saber_target: Upper body above the waist, including head and arms
Weapons.epee_target: The entire body from head to toe
Weapons.foil_target: The torso (front and back), excluding arms, legs, and head
Weapons.saber_rules: Right-of-way applies. Both cutting and thrusting are allowed. The attacker has priority -- the defender must parry before riposting to score.
Weapons.epee_rules: No right-of-way rules. Only thrusting is allowed. Simultaneous touches result in a point for both fencers. Patience and distance control are key.
Weapons.foil_rules: Right-of-way applies. Only thrusting is allowed. The attacker who initiates first has priority. Blade work and technique determine who scores.

ONama.history_1946_text: The Red Star fencing section officially came to life on November 12, 1946, and the section grew into a full club two years later. Red Star fencers quickly earned spots on the national team and diligently promoted this noble sport.
ONama.history_1960s_text: With the arrival of Vera Jeftimijades from the defunct OMK Yugoslavia, from 1960 onward the women's team dominated foil at national championships for the next decade, while the men's team became the undisputed leader in saber from 1970 forward.
ONama.history_1990_text: The club then recorded both excellent and average results, and in the nineties the red-and-white dominance of men in saber and epee was re-established, as well as that of the red-and-white ladies in foil.
ONama.values_description: The values that shape generations of Red Star fencers.
ONama.value_discipline_desc: Fencing requires concentration, control, and dedication. At Red Star, we develop discipline that extends beyond the sport.
ONama.value_spirit_desc: Respect for opponents, fair play, and honor are part of the fencing tradition that we cultivate across all generations.
ONama.value_dedication_desc: Continuous work and effort are the key to every competitor's progress. Our trainings build resilience and mental strength.
ONama.value_champions_desc: For more than seven decades, the club develops elite fencers and continues the rich sports history of Red Star.
ONama.cta_description: For more than seven decades, Red Star has been home to elite fencers and new generations of athletes.
